# Indian Cuckoo Song

<a class="gallery-back" href="../gallery.qmd">← Back to Gallery</a>

**Topic:** Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) applied to bioacoustics.
**Chapter:** [7 — Time-Frequency Analysis](../chap7.qmd)

---

## Background

The Indian Cuckoo (*Cuculus micropterus*) produces a highly stereotyped four-note call — often described as the phrase *"one more bottle"*. In the raw pressure waveform the repeated phrase is barely distinguishable by eye. The STFT maps each short frame onto a local spectrum, stacking them into a spectrogram that makes the periodic phrase and the individual note frequencies immediately visible.

The call sits in the 1–3 kHz band. Each note shows a slight downward frequency glide, and the inter-note silences appear as clean gaps in the time-frequency plane.

## Key idea

The STFT of a signal $x(t)$ with analysis window $g(t)$ is

$$
X(\tau, f) = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} x(t)\, g(t - \tau)\, e^{-j2\pi f t}\, dt
$$

The **spectrogram** is the squared magnitude $|X(\tau, f)|^2$, giving instantaneous power as a function of both time and frequency. Window length $L$ sets the time–frequency resolution trade-off: longer windows give finer frequency resolution at the cost of poorer time localisation.

## Code

```python
import numpy as np
import scipy.signal
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.io import wavfile

fs, x = wavfile.read('docs/Data/indian_cuckoo_short.wav')
x = x.astype(float) / np.iinfo(x.dtype).max   # normalise to [-1, 1]

N_window = 4096
window = scipy.signal.windows.hann(N_window, sym=True)
STFT = scipy.signal.ShortTimeFFT(window, hop=128, fs=fs,
                                  scale_to='psd', fft_mode='onesided2X')

Sxx = STFT.spectrogram(x)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(10, 6), sharex=False)

# Waveform
t = np.arange(len(x)) / fs
axes[0].plot(t, x, lw=0.5, color='steelblue')
axes[0].set_ylabel('Amplitude')
axes[0].set_xlabel('Time (s)')

# Spectrogram
t_stft = STFT.t(len(x))
f_stft = STFT.f
axes[1].pcolormesh(t_stft, f_stft / 1e3, 10 * np.log10(Sxx + 1e-12),
                   shading='gouraud', cmap='inferno', vmin=-60, vmax=0)
axes[1].set_ylim(0, 6)
axes[1].set_ylabel('Frequency (kHz)')
axes[1].set_xlabel('Time (s)')

plt.tight_layout()
```

## Result

<div class="gallery-result">
![Indian Cuckoo STFT spectrogram showing four-note phrase structure](../docs/Figure/figure_indian_cuckoo_with_bird.png)
</div>

The spectrogram reveals the four-note phrase repeating with roughly 0.5 s between calls. Each note occupies ~1.5–2.5 kHz and lasts about 0.2 s. This structure is completely invisible in the waveform alone.
